documents.title: Policy 2:3 Course Syllabus
documents.stance_why: The only AI text says 'Faculty should include a syllabus statement that outlines expectations for the use of generative artificial intelligence tools', so the rule is left to each course; it neither bans nor permits AI itself, which makes it delegates. The example statements 'reflecting different levels of expectation and limitation' are offered to adapt, not imposed.
documents.summary: Policy 2:3 on course syllabi contains a single two-sentence AI provision. Faculty should put a syllabus statement on generative AI in each syllabus, and the University will supply example statements at different levels of expectation. The policy itself sets no default for AI use.

units.why: Faculty 'should include a syllabus statement' on AI expectations: this asks instructors to communicate AI rules in the syllabus (P09), at course start. 'should' gives the modality; the content is left to the instructor, so unit_stance is neutral.
units.anchor: Faculty should include a syllabus statement that outlines expectations for the use of generative
units.resolution_why: Both coders: P09, instructor, course-start, should, neutral. Source: 'Faculty should include a syllabus statement that outlines expectations for the use of generative artificial intelligence tools in coursework.' Codes follow directly; no disagreement.

units.why: The University 'will provide example artificial intelligence syllabus statements reflecting different levels of expectation and limitation'. This is an institutional commitment to supply tiered templates, nearest to P05 (named levels); P09 does not fit because it is not the duty to state a policy. The levels are not named, so a fit_note is added.

units.fit_note: The levels are not named, and the unit is the University's promise to supply example statements, not a defined set of tiers.
units.resolution_why: Both coders: P05 with fit_note, admin, before-course, informs. Source: 'The University will provide example ... statements reflecting different levels of expectation and limitation'. A university promise of tiered examples is nearest P05; levels unnamed, so fit_note kept. Only topics differed; kept syllabus-communication and A's use-categories-levels, which describes the tiers.

notes: Both coders found that the second collected document (south-dakota-state-ctl-integrity, ctl.sdsu.edu 'AI and Academic Integrity') is a San Diego State University page (5500 Campanile Drive, San Diego), not South Dakota State; it was not coded and should be reassigned to a San Diego State record (SDSU acronym confusion). Policy 2:3 has only one AI provision (two sentences), so 2 units. No school or computing AI policy found.
